categories.title: Choices, workload and avoidable complexity
categories.diagnostic_question: Is the obstacle understanding choices, or physically reaching a target?

categories.title: Findability, predictability and information architecture
categories.diagnostic_question: Are users lost, or do they know exactly where to go but fail to activate the control?

categories.title: Visual grouping, salience and semantics
categories.diagnostic_question: Would a clearer label or grouping solve it, or is actual function broken?

categories.title: Motor interaction, target acquisition and control behavior
categories.diagnostic_question: Can users accurately acquire the action, and does its state update correctly?

categories.title: Input, validation, recovery and complexity transfer
categories.diagnostic_question: Is the input genuinely invalid, merely differently formatted or missing a clear explanation?

categories.title: Responsiveness, visibility of state and waiting
categories.diagnostic_question: Is the backend slow, or is the interface failing to communicate known state?

categories.title: First-use experience, help and learnability
categories.diagnostic_question: Can users perform first real action without reading a guide?

categories.title: Multi-step journeys, motivation and task completion
categories.diagnostic_question: Where is the emotional/operational bottleneck in the complete journey?

categories.title: User autonomy, fairness, clear consequences and credible design
categories.diagnostic_question: Can users understand and decline what the interface asks them to do?

categories.title: Inclusive, assistive-tech and modality compatibility
categories.diagnostic_question: Can people use the same essential function without a mouse, color perception or animation?

classification_rules: Label the user-observable failure, not the first plausible psychology law.
Assign one primary category and at most two secondary categories; multiple laws may explain one failure.
Distinguish confirmed observation from hypothesis or assumption. Do not claim testing when only a screenshot is available.
Use specific user goal, surface, user population, and state or device to explain impact.
Any security, data-loss, consent or accessibility blocker takes precedence over aesthetics and conversion.
When different categories overlap, prefer the category with the most directly actionable root cause.
